title: Model-variant explainability hints API (draft)
content:
Goal: design a minimal, developer-facing API surface that returns lightweight explainability hints for a chosen model variant at inference time. The hints should be: actionable (help app choose fallbacks / reranks), compact (low overhead for hosted & on-device), and privacy-aware (no PII leaks in salience).

Use cases:
- UI highlighting: show tokens/phrases that drove the model answer for user-facing provenance.
- Router / fallback decisions: if variant A and B disagree, use hints to pick the variant more likely to be grounded or confident.
- Eval sampling: collect small explainability probes across requests to detect regressions in reasoning signals when swapping quantizations.

Constraints / design principles:
- Low-cost: explainability hints must be an opt-in flag on requests; optional with tiered fidelity (none | basic | detailed).
- Compatible across model families: API should not assume transformer internals; prefer model-agnostic outputs (token-level scores, spans, short rationales).
- Small shipping: prefer compressed or token-index-based responses rather than full attention matrices.
- Privacy: strip or redact candidate spans that match known PII patterns; include a flag if redaction occurred.
- Determinism: hints should be stable for a fixed seed / prompt, but best-effort only (models may be nondeterministic).

Minimal request shape (opt-in header/query param + body):
- explainability.level: none | basic | detailed (default none)
- explainability.mode: salience | contrast | rationale | variant-diff
- explainability.max_annotations: integer (cap number of spans/token scores returned)
- explainability.sample_rate: 0..1 (for probabilistic telemetry)

Example request metadata (pseudo):
POST /v1/generate
Headers: 
  X-RW-Explain: level=basic;mode=salience;max_annotations=5;sample_rate=0.05
Body: { prompt: "Summarize the policy doc...", model: "rw-3-bert-quant-v2" }

Basic response shape (compact):
- explanation.version: v1
- explanation.model_variant: string (echoed)
- explanation.type: salience
- explanation.token_indices: [int]  # indices relative to tokenizer output (sparse)
- explanation.scores: [float]       # same length as token_indices, normalized-ish (0..1)
- explanation.aggregates: [ { span_text: string, start_idx: int, end_idx: int, score: float } ]
- explanation.redaction: none | partial | full
- explanation.notes: short string (e.g., "top tokens are generic stopwords")

Example basic response (text):
{
  explanation.version: "v1",
  explanation.model_variant: "rw-3-bert-quant-v2",
  explanation.type: "salience",
  explanation.token_indices: [3,6,7,12],
  explanation.scores: [0.48,0.22,0.18,0.12],
  explanation.aggregates: [ { span_text: "data retention policy", start_idx: 6, end_idx: 9, score: 0.6 } ],
  explanation.redaction: "partial",
  explanation.notes: "masked email-like tokens"
}

Detailed mode (costlier) adds:
- explanation.rationales: [ { text: string, confidence: float, rationale_type: token_highlight | sentence_extraction | generated_short_explanation } ]
- explanation.token_deltas: when variant-diff mode: { "base_variant": {indices/scores}, "candidate_variant": {indices/scores} } (sparse only)
- explanation.globally_normalized_score: float  # a proxy confidence aggregated over token signals
- explanation.traces: small sampling of internal signals (e.g., top-k attention heads summarized) -- textified and capped to N bytes

Variant-diff mode: returns a compact diff between two model variants when both are supplied (useful for rollouts):
- request param: explainability.mode=variant-diff & explainability.compare_to=rw-3-bert-fp16
- response: { model_variant: A, compare_to: B, delta_top_tokens: [ { token_idx, score_A, score_B, delta } ], delta_spans: [ { span_text, score_A, score_B, delta } ] }
Behavioral note: variant-diff should be sampled (not run for every request) because it doubles cost; prefer background sampling tied to sample_rate.

Sampling + telemetry:
- clients can specify explainability.sample_rate to collect signals for offline monitoring (e.g., quality drift, attention shifts).
- server should include request_id and a short explainability_id so telemetry links back to exact model/version + seed, without including full prompt content in the explain payload.

Privacy & compliance:
- Redaction step: run tokenizer pattern checks + regex PII detectors before returning spans. If a returned span contained masked PII, set explanation.redaction="partial" and include a single redaction_count integer in notes.
- Retention: when explainability.sample_rate > 0, payloads stored for diagnostics should have a retention policy and opt-out. Document must include guidance for Legal/Trust to approve storage durations.

Perf & cost controls:
- allow quota gating: explainability level restricted by plan (free-tier: basic with max_annotations=3 and sample_rate <= 0.02).
- budget-aware fallback: if a request would exceed latency SLO, runtime can drop explainability to a lighter level and add explanation.notes="downgraded_for_slo". This must be observable in console dashboards and emitted as a trace event.

Developer UX & SDK ergonomics:
- SDKs: provide a 1-liner config: client.generate({ prompt, explain: { level: 'basic', mode: 'salience' } })
- Pretty-printers: provide a helper that maps token indices back to strings using tokenizer metadata returned in the normal response (add field tokens: ["The", "quick", ...] only when client opts in with explainability.include_tokens=true)
- Consent: UI templates should show a user-facing "Explain this answer" hover that toggles a server-side flag; default off for privacy-sensitive apps.

Open questions / TODOs (low priority -> high):
- Should we return model-internal provenance ids (e.g., attention head ids) for on-prem customers only?
- How to represent explainability for models that produce non-token outputs (e.g., classifiers that output labels only)? Proposed: map label->explanatory_span as the top contributing token span.
- Compression: pick a compact binary encoding (msgpack) vs JSON; for initial rollouts JSON is fine but long-term consider gzipped sparse arrays.
- Schema versioning: include explanation.version and maintain backward compatibility for v1 -> v2 migrations.

Next steps (practical):
- Sync with console team: map explainability fields to dashboard columns (redaction, downgraded_for_slo, sample_rate).
- Implement prototype in local dev runtime with toy models (rule-based salience + synthetic rationales).
- Draft a privacy appendix for Legal & Security: describe redaction algorithms, retention defaults, and per-customer opt-out controls for Private deployments.
- Run perf microbench: measure p50/p95 cost of enabling each explainability.level on hosted small, medium, large model variants.

Notes to self: keep payloads small; prefer token-index lists over full text spans unless requested; favor sampling for expensive modes; document every place where explainability can be silently downgraded for SLO reasons so product doesn't get surprising UX.
